Summoner Spells and Runes

Pick the right two summoner spells and understand the rune page you take into every game.

What summoner spells are

Before each game you pick two summoner spells. They're extra abilities on long cooldowns (several minutes), placed on D and F by default. Almost everyone takes Flash plus one more spell that fits their role.

Every summoner spell

SpellWhat it doesWho takes it
FlashInstantly teleports you a short distance. Escape, dodge, or catch someone.Almost everyone
IgniteBurns an enemy champion with true damage and reduces their healing.Aggressive mid laners, some top laners and supports
TeleportAfter a channel, travel to an allied tower, minion or ward. Upgrades later into a faster version.Top laners, some mid laners
HealHeals you and an ally and gives move speed.Most bot laners (ADCs)
BarrierGives you a short shield.Mid laners against burst, some ADCs
ExhaustSlows an enemy and reduces their damage.Supports, sometimes mid against assassins
CleanseRemoves stuns, slows and other disables.ADCs against heavy crowd control
GhostBig move speed for a few seconds.Some fighters and tanks
SmiteBig damage to monsters. Required for jungle.Junglers only
Pro tipFlash has a 5-minute cooldown. When an enemy uses it, ping it or type the time in chat. A laner without Flash is much easier to kill for the next few minutes.

What runes are

Runes are bonuses you choose before the game in your rune page. You pick a primary tree with a powerful keystone and three more runes, a secondary tree with two runes, and three small stat shards.

The game recommends a page for each champion. That's a perfectly good place to start. Our champion guides show the most successful page for the current patch.

The five rune trees

  • Precision (attacks and long fights): keystones Press the Attack, Lethal Tempo, Fleet Footwork, Conqueror. Popular for marksmen and fighters.
  • Domination (burst and hunting): Electrocute, Dark Harvest, Hail of Blades. For assassins and burst mages.
  • Sorcery (spells and poke): Summon Aery, Arcane Comet, Stormraider's Surge, Deathfire Touch. For mages and poke champions. Minor runes include Axiom Arcanist, Manaflow Band and Gathering Storm.
  • Resolve (durability): Grasp of the Undying, Aftershock, Guardian. For tanks and supports.
  • Inspiration (utility and tricks): Glacial Augment, Unsealed Spellbook, First Strike. Creative options for experienced players.

Hover over any rune in the client to read exactly what it does.

Stat shards

The last part of a rune page is three rows of small stat bonuses:

  • Offense: Adaptive Force (AD or AP, whichever you have more of), Attack Speed, or Ability Haste.
  • Flex: Adaptive Force, Move Speed, or Health that grows with level.
  • Defense: Health, Tenacity and Slow Resist, or Health that grows with level.

If you're unsure, Adaptive Force, Adaptive Force and Health are a safe default.

Keep it simple

As a new player, make one rune page per champion you play, using the recommended or guide setup, and don't change it every game. Learn what your keystone does and play around it: for example, Electrocute rewards hitting three separate attacks or abilities quickly, so you want short, sharp combos.

Common mistakeTaking Smite when you're not the jungler, or not taking it when you are. Junglers must have Smite to clear camps and fight for objectives; everyone else should never take it.

Key takeaways

  • Take Flash plus one spell that fits your role: Teleport top, Smite jungle, Ignite or Barrier mid, Heal bot, Exhaust or Ignite support.
  • Track enemy Flash cooldowns: it's a 5-minute window to attack.
  • Rune pages have a primary tree with a keystone, a secondary tree and stat shards.
  • Start with the recommended or guide rune page and learn how your keystone works.
